title: Semihereditary topological rings give admissible condensed coefficients
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative topological ring such that every singleton is closed. Suppose every finitely generated ideal of the underlying ring $R$ is projective as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] (the semihereditary condition). Let $\Lambda$ be its continuous-function condensed ring [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], so $\Lambda(P)=C(P,R)$ for every profinite set $P$, with no restriction on the image. Then every finitely generated ideal of $R$ is finitely presented, every finitely presented $R$-module admits a finite resolution by finitely generated projective $R$-modules, and the constant-function homomorphism $R\to C(P,R)$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] for every profinite set $P$. In particular $\Lambda(*)=R$ is regular coherent and $\Lambda$ is t-admissible in the explicit sense of [def-zl-t-admissible-coefficient-models]. No completeness or local compactness of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.10, including its proof, and Lemma 6.7(1); t-admissibility is Definition 6.1. No Stacks tag states this topological-coefficient theorem.

proof.text: Every finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq R$ is projective by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-finitely-presented] to $I$: it is finitely presented. This gives coherence in the explicit meaning required here.

source.place: Lemma 6.7(1), proof, first sentence; Stacks Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective, (2) implies (1).

proof.text: For a finitely presented $R$-module $N$, [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] gives $R^m\xrightarrow{a}R^n\to N\to0$. Put $K=\operatorname{im}(a)$; the images of the $m$ coordinate vectors generate $K$. By [lem-sfb-semihereditary-finite-free-submodule], $K$ is projective. The finite free module $R^n$ is projective by the direct-summand characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] (take both maps to be the identity). Thus $0\to K\to R^n\to N\to0$ is a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives. Together with step 1 this is regular coherence.

source.place: Lemma 6.7(1), with the finite-resolution conclusion expanded using a finite presentation.

proof.text: Fix any profinite set $P$. By [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], $\Lambda(P)=C(P,R)$ with pointwise operations. Evaluation gives an $R$-linear map $e:C(P,R)\to\prod_{p\in P}R$, $e(f)_p=f(p)$, for the action by constant functions. If $e(f)=e(g)$, then $f(p)=g(p)$ for every $p$, hence $f=g$. Apply [lem-sfb-semihereditary-torsionless-flat] to this embedding. It makes $C(P,R)$ flat as an $R$-module, which is exactly flatness of the constant-function ring map by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma 6.10, proof: evaluation into the unrestricted product, followed by Chase flatness.

proof.text: Evaluation at the unique point identifies $C(*,R)$ with $R$, with inverse the constant-function map, by [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Steps 1 and 2 give the two scalar finiteness conditions of [def-zl-t-admissible-coefficient-models]; the resolution in step 2 represents $N[0]$ by its two-term finite projective complex. Step 3 holds for all profinite sets, hence for extremally disconnected ones. These are precisely the stated t-admissibility conditions. No step needs completeness, local compactness, or an image restriction on continuous functions.
